answer: The 1800-config space collapses to just 35 unique Pareto-optimal objective vectors due to massive redundancy. The Pareto front is governed by three structural properties: (1) a sharp preemption boundary in KV-cache capacity below which performance degrades severely, (2) a phase transition at max_running_reqs=256 that eliminates queueing delay on single-instance configs (e.g., TTFT drops from 12,000ms to 93ms), and (3) a fundamental tp-vs-instances trade-off where higher tensor parallelism maximizes per-GPU throughput while more instances minimize tail latency. Scheduler choice (fcfs vs sjf) and block_size (16 vs 32) have near-zero impact on the Pareto front. A structured phased search exploiting these properties achieves 100% Pareto objective recall with only 186 evaluations (10.3% of the space).
